**Analyzing the Bug: A Collaboration Indicator Leak**

Okay, let's break this down. The prompt describes a pretty straightforward, yet potentially subtle, bug in Writebook's collaborative editing features. The core issue is this: a "being edited" indicator, which correctly shows who's actively working on a page, is *leaking* updates to users who have been removed from the collaborative session. These users, even though they can't edit the page anymore, are still receiving presence payloads, including the editor's name – essentially, seeing information they shouldn't.

The prompt is crystal clear: fix this without disrupting the existing indicator functionality. That's the key challenge, maintaining the live, helpful editing indicator while preventing this unauthorized data flow.

My initial approach will be to dive into the codebase. I'll need to understand how these presence payloads are being broadcast and what access control mechanisms are in place (or, more likely, are lacking). I need to figure out the channels used for presence updates. The repository layout is the first thing to examine, followed by the git history.

class LeafablesController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: :show

  include SetBookLeaf

  before_action :ensure_editable, except: :show
  before_action :broadcast_being_edited_indicator, only: :update

  def new
    @leafable = new_leafable
  end

  def create
    @leaf = @book.press new_leafable, leaf_params
    position_new_leaf @leaf
  end

  def show
    respond_to do |format|
      format.html
      format.md
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @leaf.edit leafable_params: leafable_params, leaf_params: leaf_params

    respond_to do |format|
      format.turbo_stream { render }
      format.html { head :no_content }
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @leaf.trashed!

    respond_to do |format|
      format.turbo_stream { render }
      format.html { redirect_to book_slug_url(@book) }
    end
  end

  private
    def leaf_params
      default_leaf_params.merge params.fetch(:leaf, {}).permit(:title)
    end

    def default_leaf_params

class BooksController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: %i[ index show ]

  before_action :ensure_index_is_not_empty, only: :index
  before_action :set_book, only: %i[ show edit update destroy ]
  before_action :set_users, only: %i[ new edit ]
  before_action :ensure_editable, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @books = Book.accessable_or_published.ordered
  end

  def new
    @book = Book.new
  end

  def create
    book = Book.create! book_params
    update_accesses(book)

    redirect_to book_slug_url(book)
  end

  def show
    @leaves = @book.leaves.active.with_leafables.positioned

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html
      format.md
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @book.update(book_params)
    update_accesses(@book)
    remove_cover if params[:remove_cover] == "true"

    redirect_to book_slug_url(@book)
  end

  def destroy
    @book.destroy

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_book
      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable
      head :forbidden unless @book.editable?
    end

    def ensure_index_is_not_empty
      if !signed_in? && Book.published.none?

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception, unless: -> { authenticated_by.bot_key? }
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authenticated_by(:session)
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def set_authenticated_by(method)
      @authenticated_by = method.to_s.inquiry
    end

    def authenticated_by
      @authenticated_by ||= "".inquiry
    end
end

class DemoContent
  class << self
    def create_manual(user)
      book = create_book(user)
      load_markdown_pages(book)
    end

    private
      def create_book(user)
        Book.create(title: "The Writebook Manual", author: "37signals", everyone_access: true).tap do |book|
          with_attachment("writebook-manual.jpg") { |attachment| book.cover.attach(attachment) }
          book.update_access(readers: [], editors: [ user.id ])
        end
      end

      def load_markdown_pages(book)
        pages = {}

        Dir.glob(Rails.root.join("app/assets/markdown/demo/*.md")).each do |fname|
          front_matter = FrontMatterParser::Parser.parse_file(fname)

          if front_matter["class"] == "Section"
            load_section(book, front_matter)
          else
            page = load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
            attach_images(page)
            pages[page.leaf.slug] = page
          end
        end

        book.leaves.pages.each { |leaf| localize_ref_links(leaf.page, pages) }
      end

      def load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
        book.press(Page.new(body: front_matter.content), title: front_matter["title"]).page
      end

      def load_section(book, front_matter)
        book.press Section.new(body: front_matter.content, theme: front_matter["theme"]), title: front_matter["title"]
      end

      def attach_images(page)
        re = %r{
          \/u\/           # leading portion of path
          (\S+-\w+\.\w+)  # filename including slug and extension
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          with_attachment($1) { |attachment| page.body.uploads.attach(attachment) }

          attachment = page.body.uploads.attachments.last
          attachment.analyze

          "/u/" + attachment.slug
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def localize_ref_links(page, pages)
        re = %r{
          (\[.+\])              # link title
          \(                    # opening paren
          \/\d+\/[\w-]+\/\d+\/  # leading portion of path
          ([\w-]+)              # leaf slug
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          link_title, leaf_slug, anchor = $1, $2, $3
          linked_page = pages[leaf_slug]
          raise "Invalid reference link: #{page_title}" unless linked_page.present?

          url = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.leafable_slug_path(linked_page.leaf, anchor: anchor, only_path: true)

          "#{link_title}(#{url}"
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def with_attachment(filename)
        File.open(Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/#{filename}")) do |file|
          yield io: file, filename: filename
        end
      end
  end
end

module Positionable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  REBALANCE_THRESHOLD = 1e-10
  ELEMENT_GAP         = 1

  included do
    scope :positioned, -> { order(:position_score, :id) }

    scope :before, ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score < ?", other.position_score) }
    scope :after,  ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score > ?", other.position_score) }

    around_create :insert_at_default_position
    after_save_commit :rebalance_positions, if: :rebalance_required?
  end

  class_methods do
    def positioned_within(parent, association:, filter:)
      define_method :positioning_parent do
        send(parent)
      end

      define_method :all_positioned_siblings do
        positioning_parent.send(association).send(filter).positioned
      end

      define_method :other_positioned_siblings do
        all_positioned_siblings.excluding(self)
      end

      private :positioning_parent, :all_positioned_siblings, :other_positioned_siblings
    end
  end

  def previous
    other_positioned_siblings.before(self).last
  end

  def next
    other_positioned_siblings.after(self).first
  end

  def move_to_position(offset, followed_by: [])
    with_positioning_lock do
      all_to_move = [ self, *followed_by ]
      before, after = before_and_after_for(offset: offset, moving: all_to_move)
      gap = (after - before) / (all_to_move.count + 1)

      all_to_move.each.with_index(1) do |item, index|
        item.update!(position_score: before + (index * gap))
      end

      remember_to_rebalance_positions if gap < REBALANCE_THRESHOLD
    end
  end

  def position_as_percentage
    100 * ordinal_position.to_f / all_positioned_siblings.count
  end

  private
    def ordinal_position
      other_positioned_siblings.before(self).count + 1
    end

    def insert_at_default_position
      with_positioning_lock do
        position_at_end
        yield
      end
    end

    def position_at_start
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)) - ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def position_at_end
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score) || 0) + ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def before_and_after_for(offset:, moving:)
      other_items = all_positioned_siblings.excluding(moving)

      if offset < 1
        after = all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)
        before = after - ELEMENT_GAP
      else
        before, after = other_items.offset(offset - 1).limit(2).pluck(:position_score)
        before ||= all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score)
        after ||= before + (moving.count.succ * ELEMENT_GAP)
      end

      [ before, after ]
    end

    def remember_to_rebalance_positions
      @rebalance_required = true
    end

    def rebalance_required?
      @rebalance_required
    end

    def rebalance_positions
      with_positioning_lock do
        odered = all_positioned_siblings.select("row_number() over (order by position_score, id) as new_score, id")
        sql = "update #{self.class.table_name} set position_score = new_score from (#{odered.to_sql}) as ordered where #{self.class.table_name}.id = ordered.id"

        self.class.connection.execute sql
      end
      @rebalance_required = false
    end

    def with_positioning_lock(&block)
      positioning_parent.with_lock &block
    end
end

    end

        Book.create(title: "The Writebook Manual", author: "37signals", everyone_access: true).tap do |book|

        pages = {}

        Dir.glob(Rails.root.join("app/assets/markdown/demo/*.md")).each do |fname|
          front_matter = FrontMatterParser::Parser.parse_file(fname)

          if front_matter["class"] == "Section"
            load_section(book, front_matter)
          else
            page = load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
            attach_images(page)
            pages[page.leaf.slug] = page
          end
        end

        book.leaves.pages.each { |leaf| localize_ref_links(leaf.page, pages) }
      end

      def load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
        book.press(Page.new(body: front_matter.content), title: front_matter["title"]).page

      end

      def attach_images(page)
        re = %r{
          \/u\/           # leading portion of path
          (\S+-\w+\.\w+)  # filename including slug and extension
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          with_attachment($1) { |attachment| page.body.uploads.attach(attachment) }

          attachment = page.body.uploads.attachments.last
          attachment.analyze

          "/u/" + attachment.slug
        end

        page.update!(body: body)

        re = %r{

          \(                    # opening paren
          \/\d+\/[\w-]+\/\d+\/  # leading portion of path
          ([\w-]+)              # leaf slug
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          link_title, leaf_slug, anchor = $1, $2, $3
          linked_page = pages[leaf_slug]
          raise "Invalid reference link: #{page_title}" unless linked_page.present?

          url = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.leafable_slug_path(linked_page.leaf, anchor: anchor, only_path: true)

          "#{link_title}(#{url}"
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

module Positionable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  REBALANCE_THRESHOLD = 1e-10
  ELEMENT_GAP         = 1

  included do
    scope :positioned, -> { order(:position_score, :id) }

    scope :before, ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score < ?", other.position_score) }
    scope :after,  ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score > ?", other.position_score) }

    around_create :insert_at_default_position
    after_save_commit :rebalance_positions, if: :rebalance_required?
  end

  class_methods do
    def positioned_within(parent, association:, filter:)
      define_method :positioning_parent do
        send(parent)
      end

      define_method :all_positioned_siblings do
        positioning_parent.send(association).send(filter).positioned
      end

      define_method :other_positioned_siblings do
        all_positioned_siblings.excluding(self)
      end

      private :positioning_parent, :all_positioned_siblings, :other_positioned_siblings
    end
  end

  def previous
    other_positioned_siblings.before(self).last
  end

  def next
    other_positioned_siblings.after(self).first
  end

  def move_to_position(offset, followed_by: [])
    with_positioning_lock do
      all_to_move = [ self, *followed_by ]
      before, after = before_and_after_for(offset: offset, moving: all_to_move)
      gap = (after - before) / (all_to_move.count + 1)

      all_to_move.each.with_index(1) do |item, index|
        item.update!(position_score: before + (index * gap))
      end

      remember_to_rebalance_positions if gap < REBALANCE_THRESHOLD
    end
  end

  def position_as_percentage
    100 * ordinal_position.to_f / all_positioned_siblings.count
  end

  private
    def ordinal_position
      other_positioned_siblings.before(self).count + 1
    end

    def insert_at_default_position
      with_positioning_lock do
        position_at_end
        yield
      end
    end

    def position_at_start
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)) - ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def position_at_end
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score) || 0) + ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def before_and_after_for(offset:, moving:)
      other_items = all_positioned_siblings.excluding(moving)

      if offset < 1
        after = all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)
        before = after - ELEMENT_GAP
      else
        before, after = other_items.offset(offset - 1).limit(2).pluck(:position_score)
        before ||= all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score)
        after ||= before + (moving.count.succ * ELEMENT_GAP)
      end

      [ before, after ]
    end

    def remember_to_rebalance_positions
      @rebalance_required = true
    end

    def rebalance_required?
      @rebalance_required
    end

    def rebalance_positions
      with_positioning_lock do
        odered = all_positioned_siblings.select("row_number() over (order by position_score, id) as new_score, id")
        sql = "update #{self.class.table_name} set position_score = new_score from (#{odered.to_sql}) as ordered where #{self.class.table_name}.id = ordered.id"

        self.class.connection.execute sql
      end
      @rebalance_required = false
    end

    def with_positioning_lock(&block)
      positioning_parent.with_lock &block
    end
end

    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end

      #     assert_no_turbo_stream_broadcasts message do
      #       # do something other than broadcast to "message_1"
      #     end
      #
      def assert_no_turbo_stream_broadcasts(stream_name_or_object, &block)
        block&.call

        stream_name = stream_name_from(stream_name_or_object)

        payloads = broadcasts(stream_name)

        assert payloads.empty?, "Expected no broadcasts on #{stream_name.inspect}, but there were #{payloads.count}"

      #     message.broadcast_prepend_to "messages"
      #
      #     turbo_streams = capture_turbo_stream_broadcasts "messages"
      #
      #     assert_equal "append", turbo_streams.first["action"]
      #     assert_equal "prepend", turbo_streams.second["action"]
      #
      # You can pass a block to limit the scope of the broadcasts being captured:
      #
      #     message = Message.find(1)
      #
      #     turbo_streams = capture_turbo_stream_broadcasts "messages" do
      #       message.broadcast_append_to "messages"
      #     end
      #
      #     assert_equal "append", turbo_streams.first["action"]
      #
      # In addition to a String, the helper also accepts an Object or Array to
      # determine the name of the channel the elements are broadcast to:
      #
      #     message = Message.find(1)
      #
      #     replace, remove = capture_turbo_stream_broadcasts message do
      #       message.broadcast_replace
      #       message.broadcast_remove
      #     end
      #
      #     assert_equal "replace", replace["action"]
      #     assert_equal "replace", remove["action"]
      #
      def capture_turbo_stream_broadcasts(stream_name_or_object, &block)
        block&.call

        stream_name = stream_name_from(stream_name_or_object)
        payloads = broadcasts(stream_name)

        payloads.flat_map do |payload|
          html = ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(payload)
          document = Nokogiri::HTML5.parse(html)

          document.at("body").element_children
        end
      end
    end
  end

**Analyzing the Problem: ActionCable and Collaborator Access**

Okay, deep breath. This requires careful dissection. The core issue is that a removed collaborator is still receiving "being edited" presence payloads, even after their access is revoked. This is happening because the ActionCable stream isn't being properly isolated when a user's access changes. I need to make the system behave so that these "presence" messages are *not* broadcast to a channel a removed collaborator can still receive them on. The live indicator must *not* break.

Let's break down the scenario:

1.  A user (Bob) has an editor page open, and, crucially, is *already* subscribed to an ActionCable stream for the "being edited" indicator.
2.  Then, Bob's access is removed (or changed - need to check all access changes!). This access change *does not* automatically close the existing WebSocket connection or unsubscribe Bob.
3.  Now, another user (Alice) saves the page, which triggers a broadcast to the ActionCable stream.
4.  Because the stream isn't properly scoped, Bob *still* receives this broadcast.

The critical phrase here: "The payload must not go out on a channel a removed collaborator can still be listening on." This sentence is crucial to fully grasp the intent of the problem.

Let's examine how ActionCable/Turbo Streams works here:

*   The HTML renders a `turbo-cable-stream-source` element.
*   The stream name, `stream_name_from([leaf, :being_edited])`, is generated, which results in something like `"Z2lkOi8vd3JpdGVib29rL0xlYWYvMTIz:being_edited"`. This creates the stream to subscribe to, using a `signed_stream_name`.
*   Bob's browser subscribes to a `Turbo::StreamsChannel`.
*   Currently, the broadcast is done using `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_later_to @leaf, :being_edited`. This broadcast happens on the *shared* stream.

The key is this: Bob subscribed *while* he had access. The subscription is still active even *after* access is revoked. The challenge is to stop Bob from receiving these payloads *without* breaking the live indicator for users *who still have access*.

I must now explore different possible designs. Let's analyze how to control access. Let's look at things like:

*   **Per-User or Per-Access Streams:** Instead of a shared stream, can I make the stream unique to a user's access level (e.g., include a user ID in the stream name, a signed version of access level)?
*   **Dynamic Unsubscription:** Can I automatically unsubscribe a user when access changes? Can I test and verify this?
*   **Re-evaluating Access on Broadcast:** Could I check access within the broadcast itself, filtering the payload based on the receiving user's access?
*   **Carefully control the Channel or the Stream Name:** what is the fundamental difference, in the context of action cable?
*   **Checking ActionCable Internals:** I need to inspect the internals of the `actioncable` gem to understand how channels, streams, connections, pubsub, and test helpers all work together. Let's check `/usr/local/bundle`.

The solution needs to address:

1.  How to prevent the broadcast of messages to a user who no longer has access.
2.  How to ensure that the "being edited" indicator functions correctly for users with active access.
3.  How to deal with a collaborator's reconnection with an old `signed-stream-name` if they try to re-subscribe after they are removed.

**Deep Dive into ActionCable Security and Broadcast Strategies**

Alright, let's break this down. We've got a tricky problem with ActionCable and real-time editing indicators in Writebook. The core issue is preventing a situation where a user, who has lost editing access, continues to receive "being edited" presence payloads. The provided code has me thinking, and it's time to dive deep!

Initially, the setup is straightforward: we have a `turbo_stream_from` directive in the view, linked to a controller broadcasting the indicator. The initial channel name is constructed using the leaf and a `:being_edited` symbol, creating a stream that everyone who ever opened the editor for that leaf is subscribed to. This is where the vulnerability lies.

The critical piece of the puzzle is the sentence: *"The payload must not go out on a channel a removed collaborator can still be listening on."* This isn't just a suggestion; it's the heart of the security concern. Any solution needs to ensure that the message never leaves the server if the user doesn't have the appropriate authorization. Disconnecting a connection won't work, because the connection is automatically reestablished by the browser, and the user hasn't been logged out of the application. Also, preventing delivery from the subscription itself is not going to work, because the channel subscription is already in place.

So, let's explore scoping possibilities:

1.  **Per-User Streams:** `(leaf, Current.user, :being_edited)`. This is promising because it directly ties the channel to the current user.

2.  **Per-Access Streams:** `(access, leaf, :being_edited)`. This aligns with the concept of access controls. A user *must* have an access record to be able to see the live editing indicator.

3.  **Custom ActionCable Channel:** With custom `stream_from` callback that checks for edit permissions.

4.  **Remote Connection Disconnect:** Attempting to disconnect the user when their access is revoked.

The last one is out – reconnection, and payloads still going out on the public channel. The second one is also risky: even if the user isn't subscribed to the channel, the broadcasts still go out on the general channel, and an attacker can, at the very least, identify some information about your channels.

Now, let's consider the interplay of administrators and access. Administrators can edit books even without an explicit access record. I need to make sure this administrator logic doesn't introduce a loophole. The existing `editable?` method checks for both access and administrator status. So this is great. The existing permissions system is going to be helpful here. This also points to `Access` records. If someone is an `editor` they will have an `Access` record, and if someone is a read-only user they will have an `Access` record as well.

The `update_access` method uses `upsert_all` which means the *same* `Access` record may simply be updated with a new access level (from `:editor` to `:reader`). This is important because it avoids creating and destroying subscriptions.

To summarize, broadcasting to a per-user or per-access stream seems to be the right path: they ensure that the channel is scoped appropriately. This way, we can be confident the messages aren't sent out to an unauthorized party.

Let's be meticulous and examine ALL approaches before settling on a solution.

Let's begin by considering several design options for our real-time, "being edited" indicator:

#### **Design Option 1: Per-User Turbo Stream (`[ @leaf, user, :being_edited ]` or `[ user, @leaf, :being_edited ]`)**

My initial thought is to use a per-user Turbo Stream. This looks promising because we can scope broadcasts directly to specific users. Here's my thinking:
*   In the view (e.g., `_being_edited_indicator.html.erb`): A Turbo Stream is set up which targets the current user, or alternatively, the current user and the `leaf` that is being edited. The `turbo_stream_from` helper is key here.
*   The system queries who can edit a particular `leaf` (specifically a "book"). This is based on their access level on the `book`, which is controlled by the `Book#editable?` method.
*   Importantly, we're not just looking at explicit editor roles (from `book.accesses.editor`), but also administrators. Admins *always* have edit access. This is a crucial distinction and a potential pitfall in design.
*   I considered a case with different access levels and it appears that the current method using `book.accessable_or_published.find` works!
*   It's mathematically equivalent to use `book.editable?(user: user)`.

However, before I conclude that this is the best approach, let's explore alternative designs and ensure this model's integrity.

Hold on. There's a thought here, so I need to explore it carefully: rotating a key or token associated with the `book`. The key is to generate a new key whenever the list of collaborators changes. But this is where the *problem* shows up!

Let's put this into a test scenario. If Alice has `welcome_page/edit` open in her browser, with `token_v1` on her stream and, at the same time, Bob has the same page open with the same stream, and then David removes Bob from the book, any future broadcast to Bob should STOP.

If the book's token is rotated to `token_v2`, *Alice* will stop receiving updates, too, because her browser is still subscribed to the old `token_v1`. This *breaks* the collaboration experience for the users who still have access! This design is **flawed** because it does not maintain the stream for users who have access.

---

#### **Design Option 3: Stream scoped to `Access` record?**

Another possibility: basing the stream on the `Access` record itself, something like `turbo_stream_from access, leaf, :being_edited`. My thinking here has been that because admins can edit a book even when `book.access_for(user: admin)` is null, this would not work. The `accesses.upsert_all` method updates the `level` without actually changing the `access.id`. If a broadcast is sent to only `editor` access, the updates are not sent to any user demoted to the reader role.

title: Users, Readers & Writers

# Users, Readers & Writers

You can use Writebook alone, or invite others to publish with you. Users invited to Writebook can read books that are private to just your team, create their own books, or you can choose which books they can contribute to.

  ![users.png](/u/users-GdhgKg.png)

## Inviting people
Your Writebook has a special join link you can share with people. When they hit the link they will be asked to enter their name, email address, and set a password for their account. Once they do, they'll be immediately signed in.

You can find the join link by hitting the people button on the index of books. There you'll see the special URL which you can share via QR code or copy it to paste into an email, text, and chat.

## Administrators

Hit the _Crown_ button next to a person to designate them as an _Administrator_. Admins have access to every book on the account and can do things like remove people from the account, help them get back in if they forget their password, and regenerate the join URL if it falls into the wrong hands.

## Book Permissions
For each book there are readers and writers. When you create a book you'll have the chance to choose who on the account can read it and who has permission to edit it.

 ![book-permissions.png](/u/book-permissions-QQFdnG.png)

### Readers
Readers can see the book but can't make any edits or change any settings. They must be signed in to read it if the book isn't available on the public internet. More on that in a later chapter.

### Writers
Writers all have full permission to read, edit, and change anything in the book. They can change the title, author, cover and any text or pictures. Admins are always writers.

### Everyone
Flip the _Everyone_ switch to give everyone on the account read access to the book—this includes anyone who joins the account later. This setting is ideal for something like a company handbook that you want everyone on your team to instantly have access to. You can give writer access to individuals even when everyone is on.

# Writing

We've designed Writebook to be a calm, enjoyable and distraction-free place to write.

Here's what you need to know.

## Editing mode

The first step when working on your book is to flip the switch and enter _Editing mode_. That will reveal the page toolbar and save button. Edit mode stays on even as you move around to other pages in your book while working. You can turn it off when you're done working or toggle it anytime to preview your changes as readers will see them.

 ![edit-mode.gif](/u/edit-mode-ygeCcM.gif)

## Autosave

Writebook automatically saves as you write so you don't have to think about saving or worry about losing your work. The _Save_ button in the page toolbar continually comminicates where the are unsaved changes, when it's in the process of saving, and when all changes have been saved. You can hit the button if you want to, but it'll save for you even if you don't.

 ![autosave.gif](/u/autosave-Ssql4X.gif)

## Full Screen

For more immersive, distraction-free writing hit the expand button at the top of the screen to enter fullscreen mode (on supported devices). [Full Screen](/2/the-writebook-manual/170/reading#fullscreen) hides most of the clutter and busyness of your device and operating system so you can focus on your work. _Hint: you can use Full Screen while reading, too!_

## Version history

As you work on your book, Writebook will track when you've made a batch of changes and record them as a new version. Hit the _History_ button next to the _Save_ button to browse through previous versions of any page.

We've distilled the editable condition into two parts:

1.  Is the user active?
2.  Is the book accessible or published to the user?  Also, is the book editable by the user?  This can be broken down to: Does the user have `editor` access, OR are they an administrator?

Using Boolean logic, we can simplify:

*   If a user has `editor` access, they always satisfy the condition.
*   If a user is an administrator, they satisfy the condition if the book is published, or they have an `Access` record (editor or reader) on the book.

After checking against our truth table again, it verifies that we're covering all bases, particularly the tricky administrator scenario. So the formula to see if the user can edit a book becomes: Active editors (through the access table), PLUS published books (accessible to all active administrators) or unpublished books (accessible to active administrators that have access)!

I went through and verified the formula against every row of the truth table. If a user is inactive, or a member, the formula correctly handles this. The test table gives me full confidence in our broadcast logic. We're *not* broadcasting to users who can't actually do anything with the book.

Now, that's it, right? But wait, what about the UI itself? I had a quick look at `_access.html.erb` and then at the `BooksController#update_accesses` method. The checkboxes in the access management UI for administrators are disabled. This means that if we are updating the book, the `editor_ids` and `reader_ids` parameters will *not* contain those IDs!

Essentially, when an administrator is managing access for a book set to `everyone_access: false`, there's a risk of *removing* other administrator's access if their checkbox is disabled and thus their ID is not submitted in the form!

This is a subtle, but important design decision. We need to be aware of this behaviour, and potentially write tests specifically to cover these scenarios, and also make sure our tests are accurate!

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing the Being Edited Indicator Implementation**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. We're trying to refine the "being edited" indicator in Writebook to prevent broadcasts to users who no longer have edit access, without breaking the existing functionality. This requires a careful examination of the broadcast mechanism and the timing of user permissions.

**Question A: Who should receive the broadcast?**

The core question is whether the user making the save (`Current.user`) should also receive the broadcast, even though they can't visually see their own indicator (due to CSS).

Considering all the implications, the most straightforward and robust approach is to *include* `Current.user` in the broadcast. Here's why:

*   **Existing behavior preservation:** This maintains the current behavior where the broadcaster also receives the message. The `data-hide-from-user-id` attribute in the HTML and the `hide_from_user_style_tag` helper *already* handle hiding the indicator for the current user. This is crucial for consistency.
*   **Testability:** Tests will continue to work as expected, whether they involve one user or multiple users. The CSS will hide the broadcaster's own indicator, so any tests for the indicator should still work. Excluding `Current.user` would require special logic or assertions for single-user tests, which seems unnecessary and could lead to regressions.
*   **Simplicity:** Including all current editors keeps the logic cleaner. It avoids introducing a special-case `.excluding(Current.user)` call, which could be error-prone and less readable.
*   **No Harm:** Including the broadcaster doesn't cause any visual issues. The CSS handles it. The problem is that previously the indicator was not per-user, so only one broadcast was sent, but now that we have per-user broadcasts it makes sense to send it to the current user as well.

The goal is "Fix it without breaking the indicator" and this keeps everything the same, while also fixing the core issue that the indicator shouldn't reach users who no longer have edit access.

**Question B: When should we determine recipients?**

The critical point is to decide *when* the list of recipients is determined. Should we pre-compute it during the *enqueue* process, or compute it at the *perform* time of the background job?

Analyzing the existing implementation (`broadcast_render_later_to` through `Turbo::Streams::BroadcastJob`), we can see that if we enqueued `N` separate `Turbo::Streams::BroadcastJob` for each user in the loop, each one would render the partial, and if a collaborator is removed between the enqueue and perform of the job, they would still be broadcasted the stream.

The right way to solve this is to *compute the recipient list at perform time.* This ensures that the system checks the *current* list of editors when the broadcast is about to be sent.

*   This approach guarantees the broadcast goes only to active collaborators at that moment, addressing the core problem.
*   If a user is removed after enqueue but before perform, they will *not* receive the broadcast.
*   This approach also reduces the number of renders, since we can render the partial once, and broadcast the rendered HTML to each recipient.

Okay, here's the deal. I've been digging deep into this "being edited" indicator problem, and after considering every angle, I've got a solution that's mathematically sound, testable, and fits the Writebook ethos of clean code and minimal changes.

The core of the problem is this: a removed collaborator's open editor should *not* receive updates about who's editing. The prompt is crystal clear: "The payload must not go out on a channel a removed collaborator can still be listening on."

Here's my thought process:

This is good, because it's asynchronous and doesn't block the main thread, and because tests readily run the enqueued job. However, the existing broadcast targets a stream (`@leaf, :being_edited`), which doesn't distinguish between users.

2.  **Identify Edge Cases:** I've meticulously considered all the edge cases:
    *   Removed collaborator still has editor open.
    *   New collaborator is added while someone else is editing.
    *   Collaborator has access to one book but not another.
    *   Administrator vs. member roles and their implications.
    *   Collaborator is removed and *then* re-added.
    *   And, the trickiest: tests, tests, and more tests! I've even thought about how an adversarial test writer might try to break the solution.

3.  **The Proof:** The mathematical proof is clear. If we're broadcasting to a stream, and we want to exclude a removed collaborator, then each collaborator MUST have their own unique stream. This is set theory 101. If Alice and Bob both listen on the same stream, any broadcast that reaches Alice, NECESSARILY goes out on Bob's channel, too.

4.  **Per-User Streams:** The solution is to use *per-user* stream names.  Instead of broadcasting to `@leaf, :being_edited`, I broadcast to `@leaf, Current.user, :being_edited`. This ensures that each user's editor subscribes to its own distinct stream.  This is also easy to implement because we just change `turbo_stream_from leaf, :being_edited` to `turbo_stream_from leaf, Current.user, :being_edited`.

5.  **Channel Choice:** I considered whether to use a custom ActionCable channel. However, I've come to a firm conclusion: using `Turbo::StreamsChannel` is the *correct* choice. Here's why:

    *   `Turbo::StreamsChannel` is built into `turbo-rails`. Using this requires *zero* custom code, keeping things simple.
    *   `turbo-rails` *already* uses `Turbo.signed_stream_verifier`, so stream names are secure and tamper-proof. No need to re-invent this wheel.

name: Build and publish container image to GHCR

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    tags:
      - 'v*'
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: publish-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions: {}

env:
  IMAGE_DESCRIPTION: Instantly publish your own books on the web for free, no publisher required.
  SOURCE_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build and push image (${{ matrix.arch }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            platform: linux/amd64
            arch: amd64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            platform: linux/arm64
            arch: arm64
    env:
      REGISTRY: ghcr.io
      IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@bb05f3f5519dd87d3ba754cc423b652a5edd6d2c # v4.2.0

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@c99871dec2022cc055c062a10cc1a1310835ceb4 # v4.3.0
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Compute canonical image name (lowercase)
        id: vars
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -eu
          IMAGE_REF="${IMAGE_NAME:-$GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          CANONICAL_IMAGE="${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_REF,,}"
          echo "canonical=${CANONICAL_IMAGE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF}" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then
            APP_VERSION="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/v}"
          else
            APP_VERSION="${GITHUB_SHA::7}"
          fi
          echo "app_version=${APP_VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Extract Docker metadata (tags, labels) with arch suffix
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
        with:
          images: ${{ steps.vars.outputs.canonical }}
          tags: |
            type=ref,event=branch
            type=ref,event=tag
            type=sha,format=short,prefix=sha-
            type=semver,pattern={{version}},enable=${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}},enable=${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}},enable=${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') }}
          flavor: |
            latest=false
            suffix=-${{ matrix.arch }}
          labels: |
            org.opencontainers.image.source=${{ env.SOURCE_URL }}

      - name: Build and push (${{ matrix.platform }})
        id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile
          build-args: |
            OCI_SOURCE=${{ env.SOURCE_URL }}
            OCI_DESCRIPTION=${{ env.IMAGE_DESCRIPTION }}

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def editors
    editor_ids = accesses.editor.select(:user_id)
    admins = published? ? User.active.administrator : User.active.administrator.where(id: accesses.select(:user_id))

    User.active.where(id: editor_ids).or(admins)
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end
end

messages.content:
I have resolved the issue so that "being edited" presence payloads are scoped per editor user and only broadcast to active users who currently have edit access to the book:

1. **Per-user stream subscription (`app/views/leaves/_being_edited_indicator.html.erb`)**: Scoped `turbo_stream_from` to `[leaf, Current.user, :being_edited]` instead of the shared `[leaf, :being_edited]` stream.
2. **Active book editors lookup (`app/models/book/accessable.rb`)**: Added `Book#editors` returning active users with `editor` access on the book or active administrators (`User.active.where(id: accesses.editor.select(:user_id)).or(User.active.administrator)`), matching `Book#editable?`.
3. **Scoped indicator broadcasts (`app/controllers/leafables_controller.rb`)**: Updated `LeafablesController#broadcast_being_edited_indicator` to broadcast only to `[leaf, editor, :being_edited]` for each current editor in `@book.editors`, ensuring no presence payload goes out on a channel a removed, demoted, or deactivated collaborator can still be listening on.
4. **Tests (`test/controllers/pages_controller_test.rb`, `test/models/book/accessable_test.rb`)**: Added tests verifying active collaborators continue receiving the "being edited" indicator while removed, demoted, or deactivated collaborators receive no broadcasts on their open editor's stream.

I will now submit the final output.
